key_insight: DuSS-PET reconstructs low-dose PET images through self-supervised consistency between images and pseudo-sinograms, without paired low- and full-dose training scans.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support lower-radiation PET imaging while reducing reliance on paired training data, but clinical benefit remains unestablished.
method: Uses Bernoulli corruption in a Noisier2Noise framework to approximate low-count noise in image-derived pseudo-sinograms.
Combines an adaptive Swin transformer for pseudo-sinogram restoration with plug-and-play image enhancement.
Enforces consistency between restored pseudo-sinograms and image representations.
evidence_signal: Multi-center experiments reportedly outperform existing self-supervised methods, match or exceed supervised approaches across dose levels, and generalize across scanner vendors; the abstract provides no numerical results.
watch_item: Image-derived pseudo-sinograms approximate acquisition noise; diagnostic accuracy and prospective clinical performance require validation.
paper_title: DuSS-PET: Self-Supervised Low-Dose PET Reconstruction Using Pseudo-Dual-Domain Consistency Without Paired Data
